The stub `gh` in `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` handles `label` as a no-op (`label) : ;;` → exit 0). Note: `gh label view` would hit the `"label "*` case in permissions → `need=issues`, and the `label) : ;;` command case → exit 0. So in a stubbed test environment, `gh label view chore:pin` succeeds → `label_args` set → `--label chore:pin` appears on the `gh pr create` log line. And `gh pr edit` → `case "$cmd $2"` — `pr edit` isn't in the permission case (no `pr` pattern!), so no scope needed; `case "$cmd"` — `pr)` is NOT handled → falls to `exit 0`. So the stub would silently accept `gh pr edit` — meaning a stubbed-gh test of auto_release.sh is feasible with modest stub additions (pr list / pr create / pr edit handlers). The harness exists and is exactly the ticket's "pattern already used in repo script tests".

So the finding stands: the ticket's test plan (AC1–AC3 via stubbed gh; E1) is not landed as a checked-in test. The PR's verification was a one-off sandbox (described in prose only). AC4/REG-1 is satisfied (existing tests untouched & the pinned strings verified intact), but nothing pins the NEW behavior. Given this repo's demonstrated pattern (release_hygiene_test.dart exists precisely to pin release-flow regressions as tests, with comments like "Pin the REAL wiring ... never a script comment"), this is the strongest finding. IMPORTANT severity (not BLOCKING — the fix itself is correct and verified; CI will stay green; it's a maintainability/verification gap, not a production bug).

Hmm, let me reconsider severity per the guidelines: "IMPORTANT — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge." Yes — the ticket's own test plan asks for it ("Shell-level test with stubbed gh ... covering create / refresh / already-labeled (AC1–AC3)"). A ticket-AC gap → per formatting rule F10: "verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review". AC1/AC2/AC3 are satisfied functionally (verified manually), but the test-plan portion of the ticket is unmet. IMPORTANT.

Now let me also double-check the claim in the PR description: "`extractCreates` only matches `gh release create`, so its 'auto_release creates nothing' assertion still holds" — verified above (test line 644 asserts extractCreates(auto) isEmpty; the new script text adds `gh pr create` and `gh label view`, no `gh release create`). ✓. And `expect(auto, contains('gh pr create'))` ✓ still. `--title "Fa ` not introduced ✓. `head_version=...` pinned string intact ✓ (line unchanged). `-lt 3600` ✓. `--state closed` ✓. `git push --atomic origin main` still absent ✓. `git tag -a` absent ✓.

One more check — the CI `release` job `permissions: contents: write` — for GITHUB_TOKEN. But gh uses RELEASE_PAT, so label writes ride the PAT. The PR description addresses this. ✓.

Also check: does `gh pr edit` need `pull_requests:write`? For a classic PAT with repo scope, yes it has it. The label view needs read access — fine.

Now, another angle — `gh label view "chore:pin"` output goes to /dev/null; exit code decides. What if the repo has MORE than one label similar... irrelevant.

What about `GH_REPO`? Not set; gh infers from the git remote of cwd. The script runs at repo root (CI checkout). Other gh calls in the script rely on the same inference (`gh pr list` without --repo). ✓ consistent.

Now the third suggestion — hard-coded "chore:pin" repeated 3×. And second suggestion — self-heal via `gh label create --force || true` per repo precedent (daily_publish_report.sh:31, sweep_stale_drafts.sh:30, nightly.yml:499). Actually wait — I should double check the exact behavior the author wants: "if it is ever deleted, the script logs a loud WARNING (with the gh label create chore:pin remedy) and ships the release PR unlabeled". A self-heal create would make the warning moot. But there might be a reason the author avoided auto-create: the release job's PAT — if RELEASE_PAT lacks admin... label creation needs push/triage access, which the PAT has (it creates PRs). So auto-create is viable. But honestly the E1 scenario ("label deleted someday") — who deletes a label? Rare. Warn is fine. I'll keep SUGGESTION.

Also the identical-tree early-exit not healing labels — SUGGESTION. Let me weigh whether to include: the exhaustive-review mandate says surface everything actionable. I'll include it briefly.

Let me also sanity-check the refresh-path jq change for a subtle behavior difference: OLD: `if [ "$(gh pr list --head "$branch" --state open --json number --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" -ge 1 ]`. NEW: `open_pr=$(gh pr list ... --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true); if [ -n "$open_pr" ]`. If gh prints `[]` → old: length=0 → else-create. New: empty → else-create. Same. If gh prints two PRs (impossible per base... actually `gh pr list --head X` can return PRs to DIFFERENT bases! e.g., a PR from chore/release-vN → main AND → some other base could both exist? A head branch can have multiple open PRs to different base branches. In this repo, base is always main. Old code: any open PR ≥1 → refresh first. New code: edits `.[0]` only — same PR the old code would have skipped for. Equivalent. ✓.

Word-splitting on `$open_pr`: unquoted in echo (fine, numeric), quoted in gh call ✓.

Now — is there any BLOCKING finding? Let me think hard about whether anything could break the release flow:

1. `${label_args[@]+"${label_args[@]}"}` — verified works under set -euo pipefail with bash. CI runs `bash scripts/auto_release.sh` → bash. ✓.

2. What if `gh label view` hangs? No timeout — same as all other gh calls in this script (no timeouts anywhere). Consistent with existing style; the job has timeout-minutes: 15. ✓.

3. Could the added `gh label view` call fail under `set -e`? It's in an `if` condition — exempt. ✓.

4. Could `open_pr` contain something weird making `gh pr edit "$open_pr"` fail → warning only. ✓ never blocks.

5. Could the `gh pr edit` warning spam matter? Refresh path runs only on content change. ✓.

6. The create path with `--label` — if between the label check and create the label gets deleted → create fails with 422/404? `gh pr create --label nonexistent` → error → script dies under set -e → release blocked. - `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:30` — `gh label create "$label" … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml:499` — `gh label create nightly-red --force …`

Applying the same pattern here keeps the stated contract (labeling never blocks the release — `|| true`) while making E1 self-heal permanently instead of requiring a human to run the remediation from the WARNING:

```bash
label_args=()
gh label create "chore:pin" --force --color 1D76DB \
  --description "Machine-created release PR (auto-release)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi
```

Two side benefits:
1. `--force` is an upsert (precedented by nightly.yml), so it is idempotent when the label exists.
2. It narrows the tiny race where the label is deleted between this check and `gh pr create --label` — today that fails the create hard under `set -e`, blocking the release (the one scenario the "must never block" contract doesn't currently cover).
3. The WARNING also becomes more accurate: `gh label view` fails identically for a transient auth/network error and a truly missing label, so today's message can misdiagnose ("missing from repo") — with the create-first approach the warning only fires when even the create failed.

💡 **SUGGESTION: self-heal the label instead of warn-only (repo convention)**

The check-then-warn approach deviates from how every other label-dependent automation in this repo behaves — they all auto-create the label first:

```bash
label_args=()
gh label create "chore:pin" --force --color 1D76DB \
  --description "Machine-created release PR (auto-release)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi
```

Two side benefits:
1. `--force` is an upsert (precedented by nightly.yml), so it is idempotent when the label exists.
2. It narrows the tiny race where the label is deleted between this check and `gh pr create --label` — today that fails the create hard under `set -e`, blocking the release (the one scenario the "must never block" contract doesn't currently cover).
3. The WARNING also becomes more accurate: `gh label view` fails identically for a transient auth/network error and a truly missing label, so today's message can misdiagnose ("missing from repo") — with the create-first approach the warning only fires when even the create failed.

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Auto-release: bump the patch version, update CHANGELOG.md, open the release PR.
#
# Runs in CI on every push to main / the 2h catch-up cron (the `release` job in
# .github/workflows/ci.yml). Protected main rejects the bot's direct bump push
# ("3 of 3 required status checks are expected" — enforce_admins + strict since
# 2026-09-29), so the bump lands as a PR the machine reviews, validates and
# merges. The tag + GitHub Release are cut from the merged 'chore(release):'
# commit by scripts/tag_release.sh (the `release-tag` job) — a tag push with the
# RELEASE_PAT still fires the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
#
# Changelog rules:
# - a curated `## Unreleased` section becomes the new version's notes;
# - otherwise notes are generated from commit subjects since the last tag;
# - a fresh empty `## Unreleased` is appended at the end.
#
# Idempotent: an open release PR whose branch tree already matches the computed
# bump is left alone (the 2h cron and racing pushes re-run this harmlessly).
set -euo pipefail

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

# Coalescing guards: pub.dev rate-limits publishes (~12/day), so releases are
# capped at one per 2h; runs with nothing new since the last tag are skipped.
git fetch origin main --tags --quiet
last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then
  pending=$(git rev-list --count "$last_tag..origin/main")
  if [ "$pending" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: nothing new since $last_tag, skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag") ))
  if [ "$tag_age" -lt 7200 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: coalesced — $last_tag is ${tag_age}s old (<2h); $pending commit(s) pending. Next eligible push or the 2h cron will release them."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# One release PR at a time; and if the previous bump merged but its tag hasn't
# been cut yet (release-tag job is still running its quality gate), wait —
# tagging the next bump before the previous one would mis-tag the range.
# Keyed on the PUBSPEC VERSION, not the head commit subject: a missed
# release-tag run must not wedge auto-release forever (any interleaved or
# non-squash merge changes the subject but not the version), so after 1h the
# guard lets a fresh bump absorb the untagged one instead of blocking.
open_release_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --json headRefName \
  --jq '[.[].headRefName | select(startswith("chore/release-v"))] | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "${open_release_prs:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
  echo "Auto-release: an open release PR is already queued for the machine — skipping."
  exit 0
fi
head_version=$(git show origin/main:pubspec.yaml | sed -n 's/^version: //p')
if [ -n "$head_version" ] && ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$head_version^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  head_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct origin/main) ))
  if [ "$head_age" -lt 3600 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged (release-tag job pending, ${head_age}s old) — skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged for ${head_age}s — release-tag likely wedged; proceeding so the next range absorbs it."
fi

# chore:pin marks machine-created release PRs (gh-1134). Labeling is hygiene:
# if the label is missing from the repo, warn loudly and ship the PR anyway —
# the release is the payload, the label must never block it.
label_args=()
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi

for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  git fetch origin main
  git reset --hard origin/main

  current=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
  # Other workflows (iOS/macOS CI) tag releases without bumping pubspec —
  # when tags raced ahead, bump from the latest tag instead, or every run
  # dies on "tag already exists".
  latest_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$latest_tag" ]; then
    tag_version="${latest_tag#v}"
    if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$current" "$tag_version" | sort -V | tail -1)" = "$tag_version" ]; then
      current="$tag_version"
    fi
  fi
  IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$current"
  next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
  echo "Auto-release: v$current -> v$next (attempt $attempt)"

  last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then range="$last_tag..HEAD"; else range="HEAD"; fi
  bullets=$(git log "$range" --pretty='- %s' --no-merges | grep -v '^- chore(release):' || true)
  [ -z "$bullets" ] && bullets="- Maintenance release."

  NEXT="$next" BULLETS="$bullets" python3 - <<'PY'
import os
import re

nxt = os.environ["NEXT"]
bullets = os.environ["BULLETS"].strip()
path = "CHANGELOG.md"
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
section = f"## {nxt}\n\n{bullets}\n"

    rest = text[m.end():]
    head = re.search(r"^## ", rest, re.M)
    body = rest[: head.start()] if head else rest
    tail = rest[head.start():] if head else ""
    if body.strip():

        new_section = f"## {nxt}\n" + body.rstrip() + "\n"
    else:
        new_section = section
    text = text[: m.start()] + new_section + ("\n" + tail if tail else "")
else:
    text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n" + section

text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n## Unreleased\n"
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text)

          # the attribute, but harden the smoke test in case it ever regresses.

            xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$fa_path" 2>/dev/null || true

  release:
    name: Auto-release (bump PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Every push to main gets a release with an auto-incremented patch version
    # (0.1.x -> 0.1.y), coalesced to <=1 per 2h — pub.dev rate-limits publishes
    # (~12/day; hit on 2026-07-18). Release commits are skipped (loop guard).
    # Since 2026-09-29 protected main rejects direct bot pushes (enforce_admins
    # + strict: "3 of 3 required status checks are expected", live 14:53-21:06Z
    # failures), so this job OPENS the bump PR (scripts/auto_release.sh) and
    # the machine reviews/validates/merges it; release-tag below cuts the tag.
    # Scheduled runs catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule')
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      # auto_release.sh's gh calls (pr list / pr create) authenticate via the
      # PAT — the job env carries no GH_TOKEN by default, so without this
      # every call dies under set -e and no bump PR ever opens (BLOCK
      # finding on PR #1093, live review 2026-09-30).
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # PAT (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the publish job —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Bump version, changelog, open release PR
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # Cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release from the merged release PR (see
  # scripts/tag_release.sh). The bump now lands as a PR (protected main
  # rejects direct bot pushes), so the tag phase keys on the merged
  # 'chore(release):' squash commit instead of following the bump push
  # directly. Tag push rides RELEASE_PAT (checkout token) — GITHUB_TOKEN
  # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs. Serialized
  # with the bump PR job via the release-main group: tag first, next bump after.
  release-tag:

1. `chore:pin` is referenced in CHANGELOG.md:4204: "ci: skip SM gate bridge on chore:pin PRs — pin validation is exempt by design (#848)". So `chore:pin` is an established repo label used to skip some gate. It likely exists in the repo (created around #848). The script's defensive check handles the case it gets deleted. Good.

2. Other scripts (`daily_publish_report.sh`, `sweep_stale_drafts.sh`) follow a different convention for labels: they auto-create the label if missing (`gh label create ... --force` style). E.g.:
   - `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh:31`: `gh label create daily-publish --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \ ...` — presumably with `--force` or fallback.

So the established pattern in this codebase for label-dependent automation is self-healing auto-create (ensuring the label exists), not warn-and-degrade. The PR explicitly chose warn-not-block, with the rationale that labeling is hygiene. That's a defensible design choice and documented in the PR. But it deviates from the established self-heal pattern (`gh label create --force` is idempotent — it updates if exists, creates if missing). Actually, the author's stated reasoning: "labeling is hygiene, the release is the payload and must never block on it". An auto-create would be even better: `gh label create chore:pin --force ... || true` then always label. That's a SUGGESTION — self-heal by creating the label instead of warning. But wait — a consideration: creating labels is a repo-level mutation from a release script; the other scripts do exactly that though (daily_publish_report.sh, sweep_stale_drafts.sh create labels with || true presumably). So the repo pattern supports auto-create. I'd raise this as a SUGGESTION (or low IMPORTANT?). The PR description shows the author deliberately chose the warning path ("if it is ever deleted, the script logs a loud WARNING... and ships the release PR unlabeled — labeling is hygiene... must never block on it"). A label create with `|| true` would equally never block. Deviation from repo pattern → per guidelines G4: "Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description". 1. `gh pr create … --label "chore:pin"` at `auto_release.sh:158`.
2. Refresh path (`gh pr list` finds an open PR): idempotent `gh pr edit <n> --add-label "chore:pin"` so older label-less PRs self-heal on the next refresh.
3. Label absence must fail visibly (script logs a warning) but never block the release PR itself — labeling is hygiene, the release is the payload.

- Release flow, versioning, tag job untouched — label only.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: self-heal the label instead of warn-only (repo convention)**

The check-then-warn approach deviates from how every other label-dependent automation in this repo behaves — they all auto-create the label first:

- `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh:31` — `gh label create daily-publish … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:30` — `gh label create "$label" … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml:499` — `gh label create nightly-red --force …`

Applying the same pattern here keeps the stated contract (labeling never blocks the release — `|| true`) while making E1 self-heal permanently instead of requiring a human to run the remediation from the WARNING:

```bash
label_args=()
gh label create "chore:pin" --force --color 1D76DB \
  --description "Machine-created release PR (auto-release)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi
```

Two side benefits:
1. `--force` is an upsert (precedented by nightly.yml), so it is idempotent when the label exists.
2. It narrows the tiny race where the label is deleted between this check and `gh pr create --label` — today that fails the create hard under `set -e`, blocking the release (the one scenario the "must never block" contract doesn't currently cover).
3. The WARNING also becomes more accurate: `gh label view` fails identically for a transient auth/network error and a truly missing label, so today's message can misdiagnose ("missing from repo") — with the create-first approach the warning only fires when even the create failed.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Auto-release: bump the patch version, update CHANGELOG.md, open the release PR.
#
# Runs in CI on every push to main / the 2h catch-up cron (the `release` job in
# .github/workflows/ci.yml). Protected main rejects the bot's direct bump push
# ("3 of 3 required status checks are expected" — enforce_admins + strict since
# 2026-09-29), so the bump lands as a PR the machine reviews, validates and
# merges. The tag + GitHub Release are cut from the merged 'chore(release):'
# commit by scripts/tag_release.sh (the `release-tag` job) — a tag push with the
# RELEASE_PAT still fires the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
#
# Changelog rules:
# - a curated `## Unreleased` section becomes the new version's notes;
# - otherwise notes are generated from commit subjects since the last tag;
# - a fresh empty `## Unreleased` is appended at the end.
#
# Idempotent: an open release PR whose branch tree already matches the computed
# bump is left alone (the 2h cron and racing pushes re-run this harmlessly).
set -euo pipefail

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

# Coalescing guards: pub.dev rate-limits publishes (~12/day), so releases are
# capped at one per 2h; runs with nothing new since the last tag are skipped.
git fetch origin main --tags --quiet
last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then
  pending=$(git rev-list --count "$last_tag..origin/main")
  if [ "$pending" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: nothing new since $last_tag, skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag") ))
  if [ "$tag_age" -lt 7200 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: coalesced — $last_tag is ${tag_age}s old (<2h); $pending commit(s) pending. Next eligible push or the 2h cron will release them."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# One release PR at a time; and if the previous bump merged but its tag hasn't
# been cut yet (release-tag job is still running its quality gate), wait —
# tagging the next bump before the previous one would mis-tag the range.
# Keyed on the PUBSPEC VERSION, not the head commit subject: a missed
# release-tag run must not wedge auto-release forever (any interleaved or
# non-squash merge changes the subject but not the version), so after 1h the
# guard lets a fresh bump absorb the untagged one instead of blocking.
open_release_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --json headRefName \
  --jq '[.[].headRefName | select(startswith("chore/release-v"))] | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "${open_release_prs:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
  echo "Auto-release: an open release PR is already queued for the machine — skipping."
  exit 0
fi
head_version=$(git show origin/main:pubspec.yaml | sed -n 's/^version: //p')
if [ -n "$head_version" ] && ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$head_version^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  head_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct origin/main) ))
  if [ "$head_age" -lt 3600 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged (release-tag job pending, ${head_age}s old) — skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged for ${head_age}s — release-tag likely wedged; proceeding so the next range absorbs it."
fi

# chore:pin marks machine-created release PRs (gh-1134). Labeling is hygiene:
# if the label is missing from the repo, warn loudly and ship the PR anyway —
# the release is the payload, the label must never block it.
label_args=()
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi

for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  git fetch origin main
  git reset --hard origin/main

  current=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
  # Other workflows (iOS/macOS CI) tag releases without bumping pubspec —
  # when tags raced ahead, bump from the latest tag instead, or every run
  # dies on "tag already exists".
  latest_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$latest_tag" ]; then
    tag_version="${latest_tag#v}"
    if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$current" "$tag_version" | sort -V | tail -1)" = "$tag_version" ]; then
      current="$tag_version"
    fi
  fi
  IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$current"
  next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
  echo "Auto-release: v$current -> v$next (attempt $attempt)"

  last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then range="$last_tag..HEAD"; else range="HEAD"; fi
  bullets=$(git log "$range" --pretty='- %s' --no-merges | grep -v '^- chore(release):' || true)
  [ -z "$bullets" ] && bullets="- Maintenance release."

  NEXT="$next" BULLETS="$bullets" python3 - <<'PY'
import os
import re

nxt = os.environ["NEXT"]
bullets = os.environ["BULLETS"].strip()
path = "CHANGELOG.md"
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
section = f"## {nxt}\n\n{bullets}\n"

m = re.search(r"^## Unreleased[ \t]*$", text, re.M)
if m:
    rest = text[m.end():]
    head = re.search(r"^## ", rest, re.M)
    body = rest[: head.start()] if head else rest
    tail = rest[head.start():] if head else ""
    if body.strip():
        # Curated Unreleased content becomes this release's notes.
        new_section = f"## {nxt}\n" + body.rstrip() + "\n"
    else:
        new_section = section
    text = text[: m.start()] + new_section + ("\n" + tail if tail else "")
else:
    text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n" + section

text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n## Unreleased\n"
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text)
PY

  sed -i "s/^version: .*/version: $next/" pubspec.yaml
  # One version everywhere (gh-785): the app pubspec (Android versionName,
  # CFBundleShortVersionString fallback, App Store train) rides the same
  # bump so the ASC-approved floor can never outgrow it again.
  sed -i "s/^version: .*/version: $next+1/" flutter_app/pubspec.yaml

  git add pubspec.yaml flutter_app/pubspec.yaml CHANGELOG.md
  git commit -m "chore(release): v$next"
  branch="chore/release-v$next"

  # Rejection memory: if the machine already CLOSED a release PR for exactly
  # this bump and the tag still doesn't exist, stop — re-creating the same
  # PR every 2h forever just burns review cycles on a rejection the machine
  # already voiced. Resurrecting the release is a human decision.
  rejected=$(gh pr list --head "$branch" --state closed --json number --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  if [ "${rejected:-0}" -ge 1 ] && ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$next^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Auto-release: a release PR for $branch was already closed (machine rejection) and v$next is untagged — skipping; human decision required."
    exit 0
  fi

  # Idempotency: if the release branch already carries exactly this tree and
  # its PR is open, leave it alone (the cron would otherwise rewrite the head
  # every run and re-trigger validation + review each time).
  tree_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD^{tree})
  tree_branch=$(git ls-remote origin "refs/heads/$branch" | awk '{print $1}')
  if [ -n "$tree_branch" ]; then
    git fetch -q origin "$branch"
    tree_branch=$(git rev-parse "FETCH_HEAD^{tree}" 2>/dev/null || echo none)
  fi
  if [ "$tree_branch" = "$tree_now" ]; then

  release:
    name: Auto-release (bump PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Every push to main gets a release with an auto-incremented patch version
    # (0.1.x -> 0.1.y), coalesced to <=1 per 2h — pub.dev rate-limits publishes
    # (~12/day; hit on 2026-07-18). Release commits are skipped (loop guard).
    # Since 2026-09-29 protected main rejects direct bot pushes (enforce_admins
    # + strict: "3 of 3 required status checks are expected", live 14:53-21:06Z
    # failures), so this job OPENS the bump PR (scripts/auto_release.sh) and
    # the machine reviews/validates/merges it; release-tag below cuts the tag.
    # Scheduled runs catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule')
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      # auto_release.sh's gh calls (pr list / pr create) authenticate via the
      # PAT — the job env carries no GH_TOKEN by default, so without this
      # every call dies under set -e and no bump PR ever opens (BLOCK
      # finding on PR #1093, live review 2026-09-30).
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # PAT (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the publish job —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Bump version, changelog, open release PR
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # Cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release from the merged release PR (see
  # scripts/tag_release.sh). The bump now lands as a PR (protected main
  # rejects direct bot pushes), so the tag phase keys on the merged
  # 'chore(release):' squash commit instead of following the bump push
  # directly. Tag push rides RELEASE_PAT (checkout token) — GITHUB_TOKEN
  # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs. Serialized
  # with the bump PR job via the release-main group: tag first, next bump after.
  release-tag:

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: self-heal the label instead of warn-only (repo convention)**

The check-then-warn approach deviates from how every other label-dependent automation in this repo behaves — they all auto-create the label first:

- `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh:31` — `gh label create daily-publish … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:30` — `gh label create "$label" … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml:499` — `gh label create nightly-red --force …`

Applying the same pattern here keeps the stated contract (labeling never blocks the release — `|| true`) while making E1 self-heal permanently instead of requiring a human to run the remediation from the WARNING:

```bash
label_args=()
gh label create "chore:pin" --force --color 1D76DB \
  --description "Machine-created release PR (auto-release)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi
```

Two side benefits:
1. `--force` is an upsert (precedented by nightly.yml), so it is idempotent when the label exists.
2. It narrows the tiny race where the label is deleted between this check and `gh pr create --label` — today that fails the create hard under `set -e`, blocking the release (the one scenario the "must never block" contract doesn't currently cover).
3. The WARNING also becomes more accurate: `gh label view` fails identically for a transient auth/network error and a truly missing label, so today's message can misdiagnose ("missing from repo") — with the create-first approach the warning only fires when even the create failed.

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Fixes #1134

## What
- `gh pr create` now carries `--label chore:pin` — the flag is resolved once per run: if `chore:pin` exists in the repo, it lands on the create invocation; if it is ever deleted, the script logs a loud WARNING (with the `gh label create chore:pin` remedy) and ships the release PR unlabeled — labeling is hygiene, the release is the payload and must never block on it.
- Refresh path (branch re-pushed, PR already open) self-heals older label-less PRs via idempotent `gh pr edit <n> --add-label chore:pin`; adding an already-present label is a server-side no-op (no error, no duplicate). An edit failure warns without touching the PR.

## Why
PR #1130 shipped with zero labels: no `--label` anywhere in `scripts/auto_release.sh`, and the refresh path never added one.

## Context
- The script runs only from the ci.yml `release` job with `GH_TOKEN: RELEASE_PAT` (a PAT — label writes are permitted; no workflow `permissions:` change needed, GITHUB_TOKEN restrictions don't apply to PATs). daily-publish.yml only mentions auto_release in comments.
- Labeling only: versioning, coalescing guards, rejection memory, tag job untouched.

## Verification (no Dart touched)
- `bash -n scripts/auto_release.sh` — clean.

  - AC3 already-labeled: refresh path silent, no warning, no error ✅ (dedupe is GitHub-side idempotency)
  - E1 label deleted: WARNING logged, PR still created without `--label` ✅
- REG-1: cross-checked every string `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` pins on the script (PR-path `gh pr create`, no `git push --atomic origin main`, no `git tag -a`, no `gh release create`, bare vX.Y.Z titles, untagged guard `head_version=`/`-lt 3600`, rejection memory `--state closed`) — all intact; `extractCreates` only matches `gh release create`, so its "auto_release creates nothing" assertion still holds.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Auto-release: bump the patch version, update CHANGELOG.md, open the release PR.
#
# Runs in CI on every push to main / the 2h catch-up cron (the `release` job in
# .github/workflows/ci.yml). Protected main rejects the bot's direct bump push
# ("3 of 3 required status checks are expected" — enforce_admins + strict since
# 2026-09-29), so the bump lands as a PR the machine reviews, validates and
# merges. The tag + GitHub Release are cut from the merged 'chore(release):'
# commit by scripts/tag_release.sh (the `release-tag` job) — a tag push with the
# RELEASE_PAT still fires the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
#
# Changelog rules:
# - a curated `## Unreleased` section becomes the new version's notes;
# - otherwise notes are generated from commit subjects since the last tag;
# - a fresh empty `## Unreleased` is appended at the end.
#
# Idempotent: an open release PR whose branch tree already matches the computed
# bump is left alone (the 2h cron and racing pushes re-run this harmlessly).
set -euo pipefail

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

# Coalescing guards: pub.dev rate-limits publishes (~12/day), so releases are
# capped at one per 2h; runs with nothing new since the last tag are skipped.
git fetch origin main --tags --quiet
last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then
  pending=$(git rev-list --count "$last_tag..origin/main")
  if [ "$pending" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: nothing new since $last_tag, skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag") ))
  if [ "$tag_age" -lt 7200 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: coalesced — $last_tag is ${tag_age}s old (<2h); $pending commit(s) pending. Next eligible push or the 2h cron will release them."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# One release PR at a time; and if the previous bump merged but its tag hasn't
# been cut yet (release-tag job is still running its quality gate), wait —
# tagging the next bump before the previous one would mis-tag the range.
# Keyed on the PUBSPEC VERSION, not the head commit subject: a missed
# release-tag run must not wedge auto-release forever (any interleaved or
# non-squash merge changes the subject but not the version), so after 1h the
# guard lets a fresh bump absorb the untagged one instead of blocking.
open_release_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --json headRefName \
  --jq '[.[].headRefName | select(startswith("chore/release-v"))] | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "${open_release_prs:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
  echo "Auto-release: an open release PR is already queued for the machine — skipping."
  exit 0
fi
head_version=$(git show origin/main:pubspec.yaml | sed -n 's/^version: //p')
if [ -n "$head_version" ] && ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$head_version^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  head_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct origin/main) ))
  if [ "$head_age" -lt 3600 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged (release-tag job pending, ${head_age}s old) — skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged for ${head_age}s — release-tag likely wedged; proceeding so the next range absorbs it."
fi

# chore:pin marks machine-created release PRs (gh-1134). Labeling is hygiene:
# if the label is missing from the repo, warn loudly and ship the PR anyway —
# the release is the payload, the label must never block it.
label_args=()
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi

for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  git fetch origin main
  git reset --hard origin/main

  current=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
  # Other workflows (iOS/macOS CI) tag releases without bumping pubspec —
  # when tags raced ahead, bump from the latest tag instead, or every run
  # dies on "tag already exists".
  latest_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$latest_tag" ]; then
    tag_version="${latest_tag#v}"
    if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$current" "$tag_version" | sort -V | tail -1)" = "$tag_version" ]; then
      current="$tag_version"
    fi
  fi
  IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$current"
  next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
  echo "Auto-release: v$current -> v$next (attempt $attempt)"

  last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then range="$last_tag..HEAD"; else range="HEAD"; fi
  bullets=$(git log "$range" --pretty='- %s' --no-merges | grep -v '^- chore(release):' || true)
  [ -z "$bullets" ] && bullets="- Maintenance release."

  NEXT="$next" BULLETS="$bullets" python3 - <<'PY'
import os
import re

nxt = os.environ["NEXT"]
bullets = os.environ["BULLETS"].strip()
path = "CHANGELOG.md"
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
section = f"## {nxt}\n\n{bullets}\n"

m = re.search(r"^## Unreleased[ \t]*$", text, re.M)
if m:
    rest = text[m.end():]
    head = re.search(r"^## ", rest, re.M)
    body = rest[: head.start()] if head else rest
    tail = rest[head.start():] if head else ""
    if body.strip():
        # Curated Unreleased content becomes this release's notes.
        new_section = f"## {nxt}\n" + body.rstrip() + "\n"
    else:
        new_section = section
    text = text[: m.start()] + new_section + ("\n" + tail if tail else "")
else:
    text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n" + section

text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n## Unreleased\n"
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text)
PY

  # CFBundleShortVersionString fallback, App Store train) rides the same
  # bump so the ASC-approved floor can never outgrow it again.
  sed -i "s/^version: .*/version: $next+1/" flutter_app/pubspec.yaml

    exit 0
  fi

    git fetch -q origin "$branch"
    tree_branch=$(git rev-parse "FETCH_HEAD^{tree}" 2>/dev/null || echo none)
  fi
  if [ "$tree_branch" = "$tree_now" ]; then
    open_pr=$(gh pr list --head "$branch" --state open --json number --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    if [ "${open_pr:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
      echo "Auto-release: PR for $branch already open with identical content — nothing to do."
      exit 0
    fi
  fi

  release:
    name: Auto-release (bump PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Every push to main gets a release with an auto-incremented patch version
    # (0.1.x -> 0.1.y), coalesced to <=1 per 2h — pub.dev rate-limits publishes
    # (~12/day; hit on 2026-07-18). Release commits are skipped (loop guard).
    # Since 2026-09-29 protected main rejects direct bot pushes (enforce_admins
    # + strict: "3 of 3 required status checks are expected", live 14:53-21:06Z
    # failures), so this job OPENS the bump PR (scripts/auto_release.sh) and
    # the machine reviews/validates/merges it; release-tag below cuts the tag.
    # Scheduled runs catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule')
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      # auto_release.sh's gh calls (pr list / pr create) authenticate via the
      # PAT — the job env carries no GH_TOKEN by default, so without this
      # every call dies under set -e and no bump PR ever opens (BLOCK
      # finding on PR #1093, live review 2026-09-30).
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # PAT (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the publish job —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Bump version, changelog, open release PR
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # Cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release from the merged release PR (see
  # scripts/tag_release.sh). The bump now lands as a PR (protected main
  # rejects direct bot pushes), so the tag phase keys on the merged
  # 'chore(release):' squash commit instead of following the bump push
  # directly. Tag push rides RELEASE_PAT (checkout token) — GITHUB_TOKEN
  # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs. Serialized
  # with the bump PR job via the release-main group: tag first, next bump after.
  release-tag:

1. `gh pr create … --label "chore:pin"` at `auto_release.sh:158`.
2. Refresh path (`gh pr list` finds an open PR): idempotent `gh pr edit <n> --add-label "chore:pin"` so older label-less PRs self-heal on the next refresh.
3. Label absence must fail visibly (script logs a warning) but never block the release PR itself — labeling is hygiene, the release is the payload.

- Release flow, versioning, tag job untouched — label only.
- No new labels created; uses the existing `chore:pin`.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: self-heal the label instead of warn-only (repo convention)**

The check-then-warn approach deviates from how every other label-dependent automation in this repo behaves — they all auto-create the label first:

- `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh:31` — `gh label create daily-publish … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:30` — `gh label create "$label" … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml:499` — `gh label create nightly-red --force …`

Applying the same pattern here keeps the stated contract (labeling never blocks the release — `|| true`) while making E1 self-heal permanently instead of requiring a human to run the remediation from the WARNING:

```bash
label_args=()
gh label create "chore:pin" --force --color 1D76DB \
  --description "Machine-created release PR (auto-release)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi
```

Two side benefits:
1. `--force` is an upsert (precedented by nightly.yml), so it is idempotent when the label exists.
2. It narrows the tiny race where the label is deleted between this check and `gh pr create --label` — today that fails the create hard under `set -e`, blocking the release (the one scenario the "must never block" contract doesn't currently cover).
3. The WARNING also becomes more accurate: `gh label view` fails identically for a transient auth/network error and a truly missing label, so today's message can misdiagnose ("missing from repo") — with the create-first approach the warning only fires when even the create failed.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-30):

💡 **SUGGESTION: self-heal the label instead of warn-only (repo convention)**

The check-then-warn approach deviates from how every other label-dependent automation in this repo behaves — they all auto-create the label first:

- `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh:31` — `gh label create daily-publish … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:30` — `gh label create "$label" … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml:499` — `gh label create nightly-red --force …`

Applying the same pattern here keeps the stated contract (labeling never blocks the release — `|| true`) while making E1 self-heal permanently instead of requiring a human to run the remediation from the WARNING:

```bash
label_args=()
gh label create "chore:pin" --force --color 1D76DB \
  --description "Machine-created release PR (auto-release)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi
```

Two side benefits:
1. `--force` is an upsert (precedented by nightly.yml), so it is idempotent when the label exists.
2. It narrows the tiny race where the label is deleted between this check and `gh pr create --label` — today that fails the create hard under `set -e`, blocking the release (the one scenario the "must never block" contract doesn't currently cover).
3. The WARNING also becomes more accurate: `gh label view` fails identically for a transient auth/network error and a truly missing label, so today's message can misdiagnose ("missing from repo") — with the create-first approach the warning only fires when even the create failed.

instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Auto-release: bump the patch version, update CHANGELOG.md, open the release PR.
#
# Runs in CI on every push to main / the 2h catch-up cron (the `release` job in
# .github/workflows/ci.yml). Protected main rejects the bot's direct bump push
# ("3 of 3 required status checks are expected" — enforce_admins + strict since
# 2026-09-29), so the bump lands as a PR the machine reviews, validates and
# merges. The tag + GitHub Release are cut from the merged 'chore(release):'
# commit by scripts/tag_release.sh (the `release-tag` job) — a tag push with the
# RELEASE_PAT still fires the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
#
# Changelog rules:
# - a curated `## Unreleased` section becomes the new version's notes;
# - otherwise notes are generated from commit subjects since the last tag;
# - a fresh empty `## Unreleased` is appended at the end.
#
# Idempotent: an open release PR whose branch tree already matches the computed
# bump is left alone (the 2h cron and racing pushes re-run this harmlessly).
set -euo pipefail

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

# Coalescing guards: pub.dev rate-limits publishes (~12/day), so releases are
# capped at one per 2h; runs with nothing new since the last tag are skipped.
git fetch origin main --tags --quiet
last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then
  pending=$(git rev-list --count "$last_tag..origin/main")
  if [ "$pending" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: nothing new since $last_tag, skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag") ))
  if [ "$tag_age" -lt 7200 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: coalesced — $last_tag is ${tag_age}s old (<2h); $pending commit(s) pending. Next eligible push or the 2h cron will release them."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# One release PR at a time; and if the previous bump merged but its tag hasn't
# been cut yet (release-tag job is still running its quality gate), wait —
# tagging the next bump before the previous one would mis-tag the range.
# Keyed on the PUBSPEC VERSION, not the head commit subject: a missed
# release-tag run must not wedge auto-release forever (any interleaved or
# non-squash merge changes the subject but not the version), so after 1h the
# guard lets a fresh bump absorb the untagged one instead of blocking.
open_release_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --json headRefName \
  --jq '[.[].headRefName | select(startswith("chore/release-v"))] | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "${open_release_prs:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
  echo "Auto-release: an open release PR is already queued for the machine — skipping."
  exit 0
fi
head_version=$(git show origin/main:pubspec.yaml | sed -n 's/^version: //p')
if [ -n "$head_version" ] && ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$head_version^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  head_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct origin/main) ))
  if [ "$head_age" -lt 3600 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged (release-tag job pending, ${head_age}s old) — skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged for ${head_age}s — release-tag likely wedged; proceeding so the next range absorbs it."
fi

# chore:pin marks machine-created release PRs (gh-1134). Labeling is hygiene:
# if the label is missing from the repo, warn loudly and ship the PR anyway —
# the release is the payload, the label must never block it.
label_args=()
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi

for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  git fetch origin main
  git reset --hard origin/main

  current=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
  # Other workflows (iOS/macOS CI) tag releases without bumping pubspec —
  # when tags raced ahead, bump from the latest tag instead, or every run
  # dies on "tag already exists".
  latest_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$latest_tag" ]; then
    tag_version="${latest_tag#v}"
    if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$current" "$tag_version" | sort -V | tail -1)" = "$tag_version" ]; then
      current="$tag_version"
    fi
  fi
  IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$current"
  next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
  echo "Auto-release: v$current -> v$next (attempt $attempt)"

  last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then range="$last_tag..HEAD"; else range="HEAD"; fi
  bullets=$(git log "$range" --pretty='- %s' --no-merges | grep -v '^- chore(release):' || true)
  [ -z "$bullets" ] && bullets="- Maintenance release."

  NEXT="$next" BULLETS="$bullets" python3 - <<'PY'
import os
import re

nxt = os.environ["NEXT"]
bullets = os.environ["BULLETS"].strip()
path = "CHANGELOG.md"
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
section = f"## {nxt}\n\n{bullets}\n"

m = re.search(r"^## Unreleased[ \t]*$", text, re.M)
if m:
    rest = text[m.end():]
    head = re.search(r"^## ", rest, re.M)
    body = rest[: head.start()] if head else rest
    tail = rest[head.start():] if head else ""
    if body.strip():
        # Curated Unreleased content becomes this release's notes.
        new_section = f"## {nxt}\n" + body.rstrip() + "\n"
    else:
        new_section = section
    text = text[: m.start()] + new_section + ("\n" + tail if tail else "")
else:
    text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n" + section

text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n## Unreleased\n"
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text)
PY

  # One version everywhere (gh-785): the app pubspec (Android versionName,
  # CFBundleShortVersionString fallback, App Store train) rides the same
  # bump so the ASC-approved floor can never outgrow it again.
  sed -i "s/^version: .*/version: $next+1/" flutter_app/pubspec.yaml

  git add pubspec.yaml flutter_app/pubspec.yaml CHANGELOG.md

    exit 0
  fi

  # Idempotency: if the release branch already carries exactly this tree and
  # its PR is open, leave it alone (the cron would otherwise rewrite the head
  # every run and re-trigger validation + review each time).
  tree_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD^{tree})
  tree_branch=$(git ls-remote origin "refs/heads/$branch" | awk '{print $1}')
  if [ -n "$tree_branch" ]; then
    git fetch -q origin "$branch"
    tree_branch=$(git rev-parse "FETCH_HEAD^{tree}" 2>/dev/null || echo none)
  fi
  if [ "$tree_branch" = "$tree_now" ]; then
    open_pr=$(gh pr list --head "$branch" --state open --json number --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    if [ "${open_pr:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
      echo "Auto-release: PR for $branch already open with identical content — nothing to do."
      exit 0
    fi
  fi

    open_pr=$(gh pr list --head "$branch" --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$open_pr" ]; then
      echo "Auto-release: $branch refreshed; open PR #$open_pr now carries v$next."

Goal — auto-release PRs are created and refreshed WITH the `chore:pin` label (v1, initial)

One sentence: **`scripts/auto_release.sh` labels the automated release PR `chore:pin` on creation AND on the refresh path — today the flag is simply never passed, so every release PR (e.g. #1130) ships label-less.**

### Problem (verified, 2026-09-30)

- PR #1130 (`chore(release): v1.0.496`, machine-created) has **zero labels**.
- Root cause, exact: `scripts/auto_release.sh:158` — `gh pr create --base main --head "$branch" --title … --body …` — **no `--label` flag anywhere in the script** (`grep -n "label"` → no hits).
- The label EXISTS in the repo (`chore:pin` — `gh label list`), so this is a one-flag omission, not a label-taxonomy gap.
- The refresh path (branch re-pushed, PR already open) also never adds the label.

### Fix contract

1. `gh pr create … --label "chore:pin"` at `auto_release.sh:158`.
2. Refresh path (`gh pr list` finds an open PR): idempotent `gh pr edit <n> --add-label "chore:pin"` so older label-less PRs self-heal on the next refresh.
3. Label absence must fail visibly (script logs a warning) but never block the release PR itself — labeling is hygiene, the release is the payload.

### Backward compatibility invariants

- Release flow, versioning, tag job untouched — label only.
- No new labels created; uses the existing `chore:pin`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Fresh release branch: created PR carries `chore:pin`. (shell test or workflow dry-run on a test branch)
- **AC2** — Refresh path with an existing label-less PR: label added. 
- **AC3** — Label already present: no error, no duplicate.
- **AC4** — Regression: release flow end-to-end unchanged (existing auto-release tests green). (REG-1)

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- Shell-level test with stubbed `gh` (pattern already used in repo script tests) covering create / refresh / already-labeled (AC1–AC3).
- **REG-1** — existing auto-release workflow unchanged; a red REG blocks merge.

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Label deleted from the repo someday: warning logged, PR still created (contract 3).

## Non-goals

- No label taxonomy redesign; no auto-pin automation beyond the label.

## References

- Label-less example: PR #1130.
- Omission site: `scripts/auto_release.sh:158` (`gh pr create`), refresh branch just above it.
- Existing label: `chore:pin` (`gh label list`…

Message says "missing from repo" and prescribes `gh label create` — on a transient failure that remedy is wrong-but-harmless. Could keep `label_args` empty and warn generically, or check exit reason. Very minor. Actually the remedy is harmless; but let me think about whether to include this as a suggestion. Given the single-pass exhaustive review mandate, include it as a SUGGESTION but maybe fold into the auto-create suggestion (auto-create also fails open with || true; the warning would then only fire when even the create failed). Yes — folding is cleaner: "consider self-heal via gh label create --force || true; keep the WARNING for when the label is still absent at create time".

Actually wait. Let me reconsider: if we auto-create with `gh label create chore:pin --force ... || true`, then when label exists, create is a no-op update (with --force) — fine. When missing, it creates → label_args gets set → PR labeled. Then the warning path only fires when even create fails. This is strictly better and matches three existing precedents in-repo. But it does mutate repo config from the release script — exactly what the two other scripts already do. Is this a real gap vs the ticket? AC2 says "Refresh path with an existing label-less PR: label added." — the refresh path in the script is the "branch re-pushed with new content" path. The identical-tree early exit is arguably not a "refresh". But the practical scenario the ticket cites (#1130, label-less and open) would NOT be healed by this PR if the tree happens to match on the next run; it heals only when the bump content differs. Actually wait — would the tree match? The bump commit includes the new CHANGELOG section with generated bullets from commits since last tag. If new commits landed on main since #1130 was opened, then next run: pending>0, but coalescing: last tag is v1.0.496? The new bump commit would include newer bullets → tree differs → push → refresh path → `gh pr edit` heals. So in the common case (new commits since), the heal happens. Only in the exact-same-tree case does it skip — and then there's genuinely "nothing to do" (the PR content is identical). But the LABEL is still missing! The script's idempotency comment says "nothing to do" — yet labeling would be desirable. How likely: right after merge, the open label-less PR (#1130 for v1.0.496) + next run with no new commits → "nothing new since last tag, skipping" (pending=0 exits earlier). With new commits → tree differs → heal. So the label-less-heal-skip window is narrow (identical tree requires identical CHANGELOG content — i.e., no new commits since the branch was pushed, which the "nothing new" guard usually catches first... but not always: commits could exist while CHANGELOG bullets dedupe? No — bullets are generated from the range; new commits → different bullets → different tree. Identical tree with pending commits is only possible if the new commits are all 'chore(release):' subjects (filtered out) → bullets identical → tree identical → early exit.
