The script's idempotency comment says "nothing to do" — yet labeling would be desirable. Edge case: after THIS PR merges, the first run where tree matches exactly and PR is label-less — the PR stays unlabeled until content changes. How likely: right after merge, the open label-less PR (#1130 for v1.0.496) + next run with no new commits → "nothing new since last tag, skipping" (pending=0 exits earlier). With new commits → tree differs → heal. So the label-less-heal-skip window is narrow (identical tree requires identical CHANGELOG content — i.e., no new commits since the branch was pushed, which the "nothing new" guard usually catches first... but not always: commits could exist while CHANGELOG bullets dedupe? No — bullets are generated from the range; new commits → different bullets → different tree. Identical tree with pending commits is only possible if the new commits are all 'chore(release):' subjects (filtered out) → bullets identical → tree identical → early exit. Then the PR is for the same version and stays label-less. Rare, harmless (label-only gap, next content change heals). Worth a SUGGESTION note: move the label self-heal befo…

The stub `gh` in `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` handles `label` as a no-op (`label) : ;;` → exit 0). Note: `gh label view` would hit the `"label "*` case in permissions → `need=issues`, and the `label) : ;;` command case → exit 0. So in a stubbed test environment, `gh label view chore:pin` succeeds → `label_args` set → `--label chore:pin` appears on the `gh pr create` log line. And `gh pr edit` → `case "$cmd $2"` — `pr edit` isn't in the permission case (no `pr` pattern!), so no scope needed; `case "$cmd"` — `pr)` is NOT handled → falls to `exit 0`. So the stub would silently accept `gh pr edit` — meaning a stubbed-gh test of auto_release.sh is feasible with modest stub additions (pr list / pr create / pr edit handlers). The harness exists and is exactly the ticket's "pattern already used in repo script tests".

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: self-heal the label instead of warn-only (repo convention)**

The check-then-warn approach deviates from how every other label-dependent automation in this repo behaves — they all auto-create the label first:

- `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh:31` — `gh label create daily-publish … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:30` — `gh label create "$label" … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml:499` — `gh label create nightly-red --force …`

Applying the same pattern here keeps the stated contract (labeling never blocks the release — `|| true`) while making E1 self-heal permanently instead of requiring a human to run the remediation from the WARNING:

```bash
label_args=()
gh label create "chore:pin" --force --color 1D76DB \
  --description "Machine-created release PR (auto-release)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi
```

Two side benefits:
1. `--force` is an upsert (precedented by nightly.yml), so it is idempotent when the label exists.
2. It narrows the tiny race where the label is deleted between this check and `gh pr create --label` — today that fails the create hard under `set -e`, blocking the release (the one scenario the "must never block" contract doesn't currently cover).
3. The WARNING also becomes more accurate: `gh label view` fails identically for a transient auth/network error and a truly missing label, so today's message can misdiagnose ("missing from repo") — with the create-first approach the warning only fires when even the create failed.

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. - `gh pr create` now carries `--label chore:pin` — the flag is resolved once per run: if `chore:pin` exists in the repo, it lands on the create invocation; if it is ever deleted, the script logs a loud WARNING (with the `gh label create chore:pin` remedy) and ships the release PR unlabeled — labeling is hygiene, the release is the payload and must never block on it.

# Runs in CI on every push to main / the 2h catch-up cron (the `release` job in
# .github/workflows/ci.yml). Protected main rejects the bot's direct bump push
# ("3 of 3 required status checks are expected" — enforce_admins + strict since
# 2026-09-29), so the bump lands as a PR the machine reviews, validates and
# merges. The tag + GitHub Release are cut from the merged 'chore(release):'
# commit by scripts/tag_release.sh (the `release-tag` job) — a tag push with the
# RELEASE_PAT still fires the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
#
# Changelog rules:
# - a curated `## Unreleased` section becomes the new version's notes;
# - otherwise notes are generated from commit subjects since the last tag;
# - a fresh empty `## Unreleased` is appended at the end.
#
# Idempotent: an open release PR whose branch tree already matches the computed
# bump is left alone (the 2h cron and racing pushes re-run this harmlessly).
set -euo pipefail

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

# Coalescing guards: pub.dev rate-limits publishes (~12/day), so releases are
# capped at one per 2h; runs with nothing new since the last tag are skipped.
git fetch origin main --tags --quiet
last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then
  pending=$(git rev-list --count "$last_tag..origin/main")
  if [ "$pending" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: nothing new since $last_tag, skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag") ))
  if [ "$tag_age" -lt 7200 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: coalesced — $last_tag is ${tag_age}s old (<2h); $pending commit(s) pending. Next eligible push or the 2h cron will release them."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# One release PR at a time; and if the previous bump merged but its tag hasn't
# been cut yet (release-tag job is still running its quality gate), wait —
# tagging the next bump before the previous one would mis-tag the range.
# Keyed on the PUBSPEC VERSION, not the head commit subject: a missed
# release-tag run must not wedge auto-release forever (any interleaved or
# non-squash merge changes the subject but not the version), so after 1h the
# guard lets a fresh bump absorb the untagged one instead of blocking.
open_release_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --json headRefName \
  --jq '[.[].headRefName | select(startswith("chore/release-v"))] | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "${open_release_prs:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
  echo "Auto-release: an open release PR is already queued for the machine — skipping."
  exit 0
fi
head_version=$(git show origin/main:pubspec.yaml | sed -n 's/^version: //p')
if [ -n "$head_version" ] && ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$head_version^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  head_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct origin/main) ))
  if [ "$head_age" -lt 3600 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged (release-tag job pending, ${head_age}s old) — skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged for ${head_age}s — release-tag likely wedged; proceeding so the next range absorbs it."
fi

# chore:pin marks machine-created release PRs (gh-1134). Labeling is hygiene:
# if the label is missing from the repo, warn loudly and ship the PR anyway —
# the release is the payload, the label must never block it.
label_args=()
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi

for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  git fetch origin main
  git reset --hard origin/main

  current=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
  # Other workflows (iOS/macOS CI) tag releases without bumping pubspec —
  # when tags raced ahead, bump from the latest tag instead, or every run
  # dies on "tag already exists".
  latest_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$latest_tag" ]; then
    tag_version="${latest_tag#v}"
    if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$current" "$tag_version" | sort -V | tail -1)" = "$tag_version" ]; then
      current="$tag_version"
    fi
  fi
  IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$current"
  next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
  echo "Auto-release: v$current -> v$next (attempt $attempt)"

  last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then range="$last_tag..HEAD"; else range="HEAD"; fi
  bullets=$(git log "$range" --pretty='- %s' --no-merges | grep -v '^- chore(release):' || true)
  [ -z "$bullets" ] && bullets="- Maintenance release."

  NEXT="$next" BULLETS="$bullets" python3 - <<'PY'
import os
import re

nxt = os.environ["NEXT"]
bullets = os.environ["BULLETS"].strip()
path = "CHANGELOG.md"
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
section = f"## {nxt}\n\n{bullets}\n"

m = re.search(r"^## Unreleased[ \t]*$", text, re.M)
if m:
    rest = text[m.end():]
    head = re.search(r"^## ", rest, re.M)
    body = rest[: head.start()] if head else rest
    tail = rest[head.start():] if head else ""
    if body.strip():
        # Curated Unreleased content becomes this release's notes.
        new_section = f"## {nxt}\n" + body.rstrip() + "\n"
    else:
        new_section = section
    text = text[: m.start()] + new_section + ("\n" + tail if tail else "")
else:
    text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n" + section

text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n## Unreleased\n"
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text)
PY

  # One version everywhere (gh-785): the app pubspec (Android versionName,
  # CFBundleShortVersionString fallback, App Store train) rides the same
  # bump so the ASC-approved floor can never outgrow it again.
  sed -i "s/^version: .*/version: $next+1/" flutter_app/pubspec.yaml

  git add pubspec.yaml flutter_app/pubspec.yaml CHANGELOG.md
  git commit -m "chore(release): v$next"
  branch="chore/release-v$next"

  # Rejection memory: if the machine already CLOSED a release PR for exactly

  # PR every 2h forever just burns review cycles on a rejection the machine
  # already voiced. Resurrecting the release is a human decision.
  rejected=$(gh pr list --head "$branch" --state closed --json number --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  if [ "${rejected:-0}" -ge 1 ] && ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$next^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Auto-release: a release PR for $branch was already closed (machine rejection) and v$next is untagged — skipping; human decision required."
    exit 0
  fi

  # Idempotency: if the release branch already carries exactly this tree and
  # its PR is open, leave it alone (the cron would otherwise rewrite the head
  # every run and re-trigger validation + review each time).
  tree_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD^{tree})
  tree_branch=$(git ls-remote origin "refs/heads/$branch" | awk '{print $1}')
  if [ -n "$tree_branch" ]; then
    git fetch -q origin "$branch"
    tree_branch=$(git rev-parse "FETCH_HEAD^{tree}" 2>/dev/null || echo none)
  fi
  if [ "$tree_branch" = "$tree_now" ]; then
    open_pr=$(gh pr list --head "$branch" --state open --json number --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    if [ "${open_pr:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
      echo "Auto-release: PR for $branch already open with identical content — nothing to do."
      exit 0
    fi
  fi

  if git push --force origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$branch"; then
    open_pr=$(gh pr list --head "$branch" --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$open_pr" ]; then
      echo "Auto-release: $branch refreshed; open PR #$open_pr now carries v$next."

Actually let's think: `set -euo pipefail` is active. In the old code, if `gh pr list` failed, it would echo 0, and then `[ 0 -ge 1 ]` false → go to else → `gh pr create` → fails because PR already exists → script exits non-zero → the whole `release` job fails. In the new code, same behavior: `open_pr` empty → `gh pr create` → same. So no behavior change in error path. OK.

  release:
    name: Auto-release (bump PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Every push to main gets a release with an auto-incremented patch version
    # (0.1.x -> 0.1.y), coalesced to <=1 per 2h — pub.dev rate-limits publishes
    # (~12/day; hit on 2026-07-18). Release commits are skipped (loop guard).
    # Since 2026-09-29 protected main rejects direct bot pushes (enforce_admins
    # + strict: "3 of 3 required status checks are expected", live 14:53-21:06Z
    # failures), so this job OPENS the bump PR (scripts/auto_release.sh) and
    # the machine reviews/validates/merges it; release-tag below cuts the tag.
    # Scheduled runs catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule')
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      # auto_release.sh's gh calls (pr list / pr create) authenticate via the
      # PAT — the job env carries no GH_TOKEN by default, so without this
      # every call dies under set -e and no bump PR ever opens (BLOCK
      # finding on PR #1093, live review 2026-09-30).
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # PAT (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the publish job —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Bump version, changelog, open release PR
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # Cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release from the merged release PR (see

  # rejects direct bot pushes), so the tag phase keys on the merged

The hygiene test pins several things but there's NO test pinning the new label behavior. Goal — auto-release PRs are created and refreshed WITH the `chore:pin` label (v1, initial)

One sentence: **`scripts/auto_release.sh` labels the automated release PR `chore:pin` on creation AND on the refresh path — today the flag is simply never passed, so every release PR (e.g. #1130) ships label-less.**

### Problem (verified, 2026-09-30)

- PR #1130 (`chore(release): v1.0.496`, machine-created) has **zero labels**.
- Root cause, exact: `scripts/auto_release.sh:158` — `gh pr create --base main --head "$branch" --title … --body …` — **no `--label` flag anywhere in the script** (`grep -n "label"` → no hits).
- The label EXISTS in the repo (`chore:pin` — `gh label list`), so this is a one-flag omission, not a label-taxonomy gap.
- The refresh path (branch re-pushed, PR already open) also never adds the label.

### Fix contract

1. `gh pr create … --label "chore:pin"` at `auto_release.sh:158`.
2. Refresh path (`gh pr list` finds an open PR): idempotent `gh pr edit <n> --add-label "chore:pin"` so older label-less PRs self-heal on the next refresh.
3. Label absence must fail visibly (script logs a warning) but never block the release PR itself — labeling is hygiene, the release is the payload.

### Backward compatibility invariants

- Release flow, versioning, tag job untouched — label only.
- No new labels created; uses the existing `chore:pin`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Fresh release branch: created PR carries `chore:pin`. (shell test or workflow dry-run on a test branch)
- **AC2** — Refresh path with an existing label-less PR: label added. 
- **AC3** — Label already present: no error, no duplicate.
- **AC4** — Regression: release flow end-to-end unchanged (existing auto-release tests green). (REG-1)

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- Shell-level test with stubbed `gh` (pattern already used in repo script tests) covering create / refresh / already-labeled (AC1–AC3).
- **REG-1** — existing auto-release workflow unchanged; a red REG blocks merge.

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Label deleted from the repo someday: warning logged, PR still created (contract 3).

## Non-goals

- No label taxonomy redesign; no auto-pin automation beyond the label.

## References

- Label-less example: PR #1130.
- Omission site: `scripts/auto_release.sh:158` (`gh pr create`), refresh branch just above it.
- Existing label: `chore:pin` (`gh label list`…

The stub `gh` in `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` handles `label` as a no-op (`label) : ;;` → exit 0). Note: `gh label view` would hit the `"label "*` case in permissions → `need=issues`, and the `label) : ;;` command case → exit 0. So in a stubbed test environment, `gh label view chore:pin` succeeds → `label_args` set → `--label chore:pin` appears on the `gh pr create` log line. And `gh pr edit` → `case "$cmd $2"` — `pr edit` isn't in the permission case (no `pr` pattern!), so no scope needed; `case "$cmd"` — `pr)` is NOT handled → falls to `exit 0`. So the stub would silently accept `gh pr edit` — meaning a stubbed-gh test of auto_release.sh is feasible with modest stub additions (pr list / pr create / pr edit handlers). The harness exists and is exactly the ticket's "pattern already used in repo script tests".

So the finding stands: the ticket's test plan (AC1–AC3 via stubbed gh; E1) is not landed as a checked-in test. The PR's verification was a one-off sandbox (described in prose only). AC4/REG-1 is satisfied (existing tests untouched & the pinned strings verified intact), but nothing pins the NEW behavior. Given this repo's demonstrated pattern (release_hygiene_test.dart exists precisely to pin release-flow regressions as tests, with comments like "Pin the REAL wiring ... never a script comment"), this is the strongest finding. IMPORTANT severity (not BLOCKING — the fix itself is correct and verified; CI will stay green; it's a maintainability/verification gap, not a production bug).

Now, another angle — `gh label view "chore:pin"` output goes to /dev/null; exit code decides. What if the repo has MORE than one label similar... irrelevant.

NEW: `open_pr=$(gh pr list ... --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true); if [ -n "$open_pr" ]`. If gh prints `[]` → old: length=0 → else-create. New: empty → else-create. Same. New code: edits `.[0]` only — same PR the old code would have skipped for. Equivalent. ✓.

Word-splitting on `$open_pr`: unquoted in echo (fine, numeric), quoted in gh call ✓.

Now — is there any BLOCKING finding? Let me think hard about whether anything could break the release flow:

The create path with `--label` — if between the label check and create the label gets deleted → create fails with 422/404? `gh pr create --label nonexistent` → error → script dies under set -e → release blocked. Race window is seconds; the design accepts it (label exists; deletion mid-run is vanishingly rare). Not worth flagging... actually it contradicts "the label must never block the release" in an ultra-rare race. The self-heal suggestion (create-if-missing right before use) would narrow it further. I'll fold into the suggestion comment.

if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi
```

Two side benefits:
1. `--force` is an upsert (precedented by nightly.yml), so it is idempotent when the label exists.
2. It narrows the tiny race where the label is deleted between this check and `gh pr create --label` — today that fails the create hard under `set -e`, blocking the release (the one scenario the "must never block" contract doesn't currently cover).
3. The WARNING also becomes more accurate: `gh label view` fails identically for a transient auth/network error and a truly missing label, so today's message can misdiagnose ("missing from repo") — with the create-first approach the warning only fires when even the create failed.

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Auto-release: bump the patch version, update CHANGELOG.md, open the release PR.
#
# Runs in CI on every push to main / the 2h catch-up cron (the `release` job in
# .github/workflows/ci.yml). Protected main rejects the bot's direct bump push
# ("3 of 3 required status checks are expected" — enforce_admins + strict since
# 2026-09-29), so the bump lands as a PR the machine reviews, validates and
# merges. The tag + GitHub Release are cut from the merged 'chore(release):'
# commit by scripts/tag_release.sh (the `release-tag` job) — a tag push with the
# RELEASE_PAT still fires the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
#
# Changelog rules:
# - a curated `## Unreleased` section becomes the new version's notes;
# - otherwise notes are generated from commit subjects since the last tag;
# - a fresh empty `## Unreleased` is appended at the end.
#
# Idempotent: an open release PR whose branch tree already matches the computed
# bump is left alone (the 2h cron and racing pushes re-run this harmlessly).
set -euo pipefail

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

# Coalescing guards: pub.dev rate-limits publishes (~12/day), so releases are
# capped at one per 2h; runs with nothing new since the last tag are skipped.
git fetch origin main --tags --quiet
last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then
  pending=$(git rev-list --count "$last_tag..origin/main")
  if [ "$pending" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: nothing new since $last_tag, skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag") ))
  if [ "$tag_age" -lt 7200 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: coalesced — $last_tag is ${tag_age}s old (<2h); $pending commit(s) pending. Next eligible push or the 2h cron will release them."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# One release PR at a time; and if the previous bump merged but its tag hasn't
# been cut yet (release-tag job is still running its quality gate), wait —
# tagging the next bump before the previous one would mis-tag the range.
# Keyed on the PUBSPEC VERSION, not the head commit subject: a missed
# release-tag run must not wedge auto-release forever (any interleaved or
# non-squash merge changes the subject but not the version), so after 1h the
# guard lets a fresh bump absorb the untagged one instead of blocking.
open_release_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --json headRefName \
  --jq '[.[].headRefName | select(startswith("chore/release-v"))] | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "${open_release_prs:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
  echo "Auto-release: an open release PR is already queued for the machine — skipping."
  exit 0
fi
head_version=$(git show origin/main:pubspec.yaml | sed -n 's/^version: //p')
if [ -n "$head_version" ] && ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$head_version^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  head_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct origin/main) ))
  if [ "$head_age" -lt 3600 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged (release-tag job pending, ${head_age}s old) — skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged for ${head_age}s — release-tag likely wedged; proceeding so the next range absorbs it."
fi

# chore:pin marks machine-created release PRs (gh-1134). Labeling is hygiene:
# if the label is missing from the repo, warn loudly and ship the PR anyway —
# the release is the payload, the label must never block it.
label_args=()
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi

for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  git fetch origin main
  git reset --hard origin/main

  current=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
  # Other workflows (iOS/macOS CI) tag releases without bumping pubspec —
  # when tags raced ahead, bump from the latest tag instead, or every run
  # dies on "tag already exists".
  latest_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$latest_tag" ]; then
    tag_version="${latest_tag#v}"
    if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$current" "$tag_version" | sort -V | tail -1)" = "$tag_version" ]; then
      current="$tag_version"
    fi
  fi
  IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$current"
  next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
  echo "Auto-release: v$current -> v$next (attempt $attempt)"

  last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then range="$last_tag..HEAD"; else range="HEAD"; fi
  bullets=$(git log "$range" --pretty='- %s' --no-merges | grep -v '^- chore(release):' || true)
  [ -z "$bullets" ] && bullets="- Maintenance release."

  NEXT="$next" BULLETS="$bullets" python3 - <<'PY'
import os
import re

nxt = os.environ["NEXT"]
bullets = os.environ["BULLETS"].strip()
path = "CHANGELOG.md"
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
section = f"## {nxt}\n\n{bullets}\n"

m = re.search(r"^## Unreleased[ \t]*$", text, re.M)
if m:
    rest = text[m.end():]
    head = re.search(r"^## ", rest, re.M)
    body = rest[: head.start()] if head else rest
    tail = rest[head.start():] if head else ""
    if body.strip():
        # Curated Unreleased content becomes this release's notes.
        new_section = f"## {nxt}\n" + body.rstrip() + "\n"
    else:
        new_section = section
    text = text[: m.start()] + new_section + ("\n" + tail if tail else "")
else:
    text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n" + section

text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n## Unreleased\n"
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text)
PY

  release:
    name: Auto-release (bump PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Every push to main gets a release with an auto-incremented patch version
    # (0.1.x -> 0.1.y), coalesced to <=1 per 2h — pub.dev rate-limits publishes
    # (~12/day; hit on 2026-07-18). Release commits are skipped (loop guard).
    # Since 2026-09-29 protected main rejects direct bot pushes (enforce_admins
    # + strict: "3 of 3 required status checks are expected", live 14:53-21:06Z
    # failures), so this job OPENS the bump PR (scripts/auto_release.sh) and
    # the machine reviews/validates/merges it; release-tag below cuts the tag.
    # Scheduled runs catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule')
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      # auto_release.sh's gh calls (pr list / pr create) authenticate via the
      # PAT — the job env carries no GH_TOKEN by default, so without this
      # every call dies under set -e and no bump PR ever opens (BLOCK
      # finding on PR #1093, live review 2026-09-30).
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # PAT (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the publish job —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Bump version, changelog, open release PR
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # Cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release from the merged release PR (see
  # scripts/tag_release.sh). The bump now lands as a PR (protected main
  # rejects direct bot pushes), so the tag phase keys on the merged
  # 'chore(release):' squash commit instead of following the bump push
  # directly. Tag push rides RELEASE_PAT (checkout token) — GITHUB_TOKEN
  # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs. Serialized
  # with the bump PR job via the release-main group: tag first, next bump after.
  release-tag:

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: self-heal the label instead of warn-only (repo convention)**

The check-then-warn approach deviates from how every other label-dependent automation in this repo behaves — they all auto-create the label first:

- `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh:31` — `gh label create daily-publish … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:30` — `gh label create "$label" … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml:499` — `gh label create nightly-red --force …`

Applying the same pattern here keeps the stated contract (labeling never blocks the release — `|| true`) while making E1 self-heal permanently instead of requiring a human to run the remediation from the WARNING:

```bash
label_args=()
gh label create "chore:pin" --force --color 1D76DB \
  --description "Machine-created release PR (auto-release)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi
```

Two side benefits:
1. `--force` is an upsert (precedented by nightly.yml), so it is idempotent when the label exists.
2. It narrows the tiny race where the label is deleted between this check and `gh pr create --label` — today that fails the create hard under `set -e`, blocking the release (the one scenario the "must never block" contract doesn't currently cover).
3. The WARNING also becomes more accurate: `gh label view` fails identically for a transient auth/network error and a truly missing label, so today's message can misdiagnose ("missing from repo") — with the create-first approach the warning only fires when even the create failed.

# Auto-release: bump the patch version, update CHANGELOG.md, open the release PR.
#
# Runs in CI on every push to main / the 2h catch-up cron (the `release` job in
# .github/workflows/ci.yml). Protected main rejects the bot's direct bump push
# ("3 of 3 required status checks are expected" — enforce_admins + strict since
# 2026-09-29), so the bump lands as a PR the machine reviews, validates and

# - otherwise notes are generated from commit subjects since the last tag;
# - a fresh empty `## Unreleased` is appended at the end.

    name: Auto-release (bump PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Every push to main gets a release with an auto-incremented patch version
    # (0.1.x -> 0.1.y), coalesced to <=1 per 2h — pub.dev rate-limits publishes

    # + strict: "3 of 3 required status checks are expected", live 14:53-21:06Z
    # failures), so this job OPENS the bump PR (scripts/auto_release.sh) and
    # the machine reviews/validates/merges it; release-tag below cuts the tag.
    # Scheduled runs catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    if: >-

      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule')

Goal — auto-release PRs are created and refreshed WITH the `chore:pin` label (v1, initial)

One sentence: **`scripts/auto_release.sh` labels the automated release PR `chore:pin` on creation AND on the refresh path — today the flag is simply never passed, so every release PR (e.g. #1130) ships label-less.**

### Problem (verified, 2026-09-30)

- PR #1130 (`chore(release): v1.0.496`, machine-created) has **zero labels**.
- Root cause, exact: `scripts/auto_release.sh:158` — `gh pr create --base main --head "$branch" --title … --body …` — **no `--label` flag anywhere in the script** (`grep -n "label"` → no hits).
- The label EXISTS in the repo (`chore:pin` — `gh label list`), so this is a one-flag omission, not a label-taxonomy gap.
- The refresh path (branch re-pushed, PR already open) also never adds the label.

### Fix contract

1. `gh pr create … --label "chore:pin"` at `auto_release.sh:158`.
2. Refresh path (`gh pr list` finds an open PR): idempotent `gh pr edit <n> --add-label "chore:pin"` so older label-less PRs self-heal on the next refresh.
3. Label absence must fail visibly (script logs a warning) but never block the release PR itself — labeling is hygiene, the release is the payload.

### Backward compatibility invariants

- Release flow, versioning, tag job untouched — label only.
- No new labels created; uses the existing `chore:pin`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Fresh release branch: created PR carries `chore:pin`. (shell test or workflow dry-run on a test branch)
- **AC2** — Refresh path with an existing label-less PR: label added. 
- **AC3** — Label already present: no error, no duplicate.
- **AC4** — Regression: release flow end-to-end unchanged (existing auto-release tests green). (REG-1)

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- Shell-level test with stubbed `gh` (pattern already used in repo script tests) covering create / refresh / already-labeled (AC1–AC3).
- **REG-1** — existing auto-release workflow unchanged; a red REG blocks merge.

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Label deleted from the repo someday: warning logged, PR still created (contract 3).

## Non-goals

- No label taxonomy redesign; no auto-pin automation beyond the label.

## References

- Label-less example: PR #1130.
- Omission site: `scripts/auto_release.sh:158` (`gh pr create`), refresh branch just above it.
- Existing label: `chore:pin` (`gh label list`…

The stub `gh` in `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` handles `label` as a no-op (`label) : ;;` → exit 0). Note: `gh label view` would hit the `"label "*` case in permissions → `need=issues`, and the `label) : ;;` command case → exit 0. So in a stubbed test environment, `gh label view chore:pin` succeeds → `label_args` set → `--label chore:pin` appears on the `gh pr create` log line. And `gh pr edit` → `case "$cmd $2"` — `pr edit` isn't in the permission case (no `pr` pattern!), so no scope needed; `case "$cmd"` — `pr)` is NOT handled → falls to `exit 0`. So the stub would silently accept `gh pr edit` — meaning a stubbed-gh test of auto_release.sh is feasible with modest stub additions (pr list / pr create / pr edit handlers). The harness exists and is exactly the ticket's "pattern already used in repo script tests".

So the finding stands: the ticket's test plan (AC1–AC3 via stubbed gh; E1) is not landed as a checked-in test. The PR's verification was a one-off sandbox (described in prose only). AC4/REG-1 is satisfied (existing tests untouched & the pinned strings verified intact), but nothing pins the NEW behavior. Given this repo's demonstrated pattern (release_hygiene_test.dart exists precisely to pin release-flow regressions as tests, with comments like "Pin the REAL wiring ... never a script comment"), this is the strongest finding. IMPORTANT severity (not BLOCKING — the fix itself is correct and verified; CI will stay green; it's a maintainability/verification gap, not a production bug).

Now, another angle — `gh label view "chore:pin"` output goes to /dev/null; exit code decides. What if the repo has MORE than one label similar... irrelevant.

NEW: `open_pr=$(gh pr list ... --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true); if [ -n "$open_pr" ]`. If gh prints `[]` → old: length=0 → else-create. New: empty → else-create. Same. New code: edits `.[0]` only — same PR the old code would have skipped for. Equivalent. ✓.

Word-splitting on `$open_pr`: unquoted in echo (fine, numeric), quoted in gh call ✓.

Now — is there any BLOCKING finding? Let me think hard about whether anything could break the release flow:

The create path with `--label` — if between the label check and create the label gets deleted → create fails with 422/404? `gh pr create --label nonexistent` → error → script dies under set -e → release blocked. Race window is seconds; the design accepts it (label exists; deletion mid-run is vanishingly rare). Not worth flagging... actually it contradicts "the label must never block the release" in an ultra-rare race. The self-heal suggestion (create-if-missing right before use) would narrow it further. I'll fold into the suggestion comment.

if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi
```

Two side benefits:
1. `--force` is an upsert (precedented by nightly.yml), so it is idempotent when the label exists.
2. It narrows the tiny race where the label is deleted between this check and `gh pr create --label` — today that fails the create hard under `set -e`, blocking the release (the one scenario the "must never block" contract doesn't currently cover).
3. The WARNING also becomes more accurate: `gh label view` fails identically for a transient auth/network error and a truly missing label, so today's message can misdiagnose ("missing from repo") — with the create-first approach the warning only fires when even the create failed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Auto-release: bump the patch version, update CHANGELOG.md, open the release PR.
#
# Runs in CI on every push to main / the 2h catch-up cron (the `release` job in
# .github/workflows/ci.yml). Protected main rejects the bot's direct bump push
# ("3 of 3 required status checks are expected" — enforce_admins + strict since
# 2026-09-29), so the bump lands as a PR the machine reviews, validates and
# merges. The tag + GitHub Release are cut from the merged 'chore(release):'
# commit by scripts/tag_release.sh (the `release-tag` job) — a tag push with the
# RELEASE_PAT still fires the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
#
# Changelog rules:
# - a curated `## Unreleased` section becomes the new version's notes;
# - otherwise notes are generated from commit subjects since the last tag;
# - a fresh empty `## Unreleased` is appended at the end.
#
# Idempotent: an open release PR whose branch tree already matches the computed
# bump is left alone (the 2h cron and racing pushes re-run this harmlessly).
set -euo pipefail

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

# Coalescing guards: pub.dev rate-limits publishes (~12/day), so releases are
# capped at one per 2h; runs with nothing new since the last tag are skipped.
git fetch origin main --tags --quiet
last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then
  pending=$(git rev-list --count "$last_tag..origin/main")
  if [ "$pending" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: nothing new since $last_tag, skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag") ))
  if [ "$tag_age" -lt 7200 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: coalesced — $last_tag is ${tag_age}s old (<2h); $pending commit(s) pending. Next eligible push or the 2h cron will release them."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# One release PR at a time; and if the previous bump merged but its tag hasn't
# been cut yet (release-tag job is still running its quality gate), wait —
# tagging the next bump before the previous one would mis-tag the range.
# Keyed on the PUBSPEC VERSION, not the head commit subject: a missed
# release-tag run must not wedge auto-release forever (any interleaved or
# non-squash merge changes the subject but not the version), so after 1h the
# guard lets a fresh bump absorb the untagged one instead of blocking.
open_release_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --json headRefName \
  --jq '[.[].headRefName | select(startswith("chore/release-v"))] | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "${open_release_prs:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
  echo "Auto-release: an open release PR is already queued for the machine — skipping."
  exit 0
fi
head_version=$(git show origin/main:pubspec.yaml | sed -n 's/^version: //p')
if [ -n "$head_version" ] && ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$head_version^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  head_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct origin/main) ))
  if [ "$head_age" -lt 3600 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged (release-tag job pending, ${head_age}s old) — skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged for ${head_age}s — release-tag likely wedged; proceeding so the next range absorbs it."
fi

# chore:pin marks machine-created release PRs (gh-1134). Labeling is hygiene:
# if the label is missing from the repo, warn loudly and ship the PR anyway —
# the release is the payload, the label must never block it.
label_args=()
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi

for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  git fetch origin main
  git reset --hard origin/main

  current=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
  # Other workflows (iOS/macOS CI) tag releases without bumping pubspec —
  # when tags raced ahead, bump from the latest tag instead, or every run
  # dies on "tag already exists".
  latest_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$latest_tag" ]; then
    tag_version="${latest_tag#v}"
    if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$current" "$tag_version" | sort -V | tail -1)" = "$tag_version" ]; then
      current="$tag_version"
    fi
  fi
  IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$current"
  next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
  echo "Auto-release: v$current -> v$next (attempt $attempt)"

  last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then range="$last_tag..HEAD"; else range="HEAD"; fi
  bullets=$(git log "$range" --pretty='- %s' --no-merges | grep -v '^- chore(release):' || true)
  [ -z "$bullets" ] && bullets="- Maintenance release."

  NEXT="$next" BULLETS="$bullets" python3 - <<'PY'

import re

bullets = os.environ["BULLETS"].strip()
path = "CHANGELOG.md"

    tail = rest[head.start():] if head else ""

  release:
    name: Auto-release (bump PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Every push to main gets a release with an auto-incremented patch version
    # (0.1.x -> 0.1.y), coalesced to <=1 per 2h — pub.dev rate-limits publishes
    # (~12/day; hit on 2026-07-18). Release commits are skipped (loop guard).
    # Since 2026-09-29 protected main rejects direct bot pushes (enforce_admins
    # + strict: "3 of 3 required status checks are expected", live 14:53-21:06Z
    # failures), so this job OPENS the bump PR (scripts/auto_release.sh) and
    # the machine reviews/validates/merges it; release-tag below cuts the tag.
    # Scheduled runs catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule')
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      # auto_release.sh's gh calls (pr list / pr create) authenticate via the
      # PAT — the job env carries no GH_TOKEN by default, so without this
      # every call dies under set -e and no bump PR ever opens (BLOCK
      # finding on PR #1093, live review 2026-09-30).
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # PAT (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the publish job —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Bump version, changelog, open release PR
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # Cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release from the merged release PR (see
  # scripts/tag_release.sh). The bump now lands as a PR (protected main
  # rejects direct bot pushes), so the tag phase keys on the merged
  # 'chore(release):' squash commit instead of following the bump push
  # directly. Tag push rides RELEASE_PAT (checkout token) — GITHUB_TOKEN
  # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs. Serialized
  # with the bump PR job via the release-main group: tag first, next bump after.
  release-tag:

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: self-heal the label instead of warn-only (repo convention)**

The check-then-warn approach deviates from how every other label-dependent automation in this repo behaves — they all auto-create the label first:

- `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh:31` — `gh label create daily-publish … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:30` — `gh label create "$label" … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml:499` — `gh label create nightly-red --force …`

Applying the same pattern here keeps the stated contract (labeling never blocks the release — `|| true`) while making E1 self-heal permanently instead of requiring a human to run the remediation from the WARNING:

```bash
label_args=()
gh label create "chore:pin" --force --color 1D76DB \
  --description "Machine-created release PR (auto-release)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi
```

Two side benefits:
1. `--force` is an upsert (precedented by nightly.yml), so it is idempotent when the label exists.
2. It narrows the tiny race where the label is deleted between this check and `gh pr create --label` — today that fails the create hard under `set -e`, blocking the release (the one scenario the "must never block" contract doesn't currently cover).
3. The WARNING also becomes more accurate: `gh label view` fails identically for a transient auth/network error and a truly missing label, so today's message can misdiagnose ("missing from repo") — with the create-first approach the warning only fires when even the create failed.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Auto-release: bump the patch version, update CHANGELOG.md, open the release PR.
#
# Runs in CI on every push to main / the 2h catch-up cron (the `release` job in
# .github/workflows/ci.yml). Protected main rejects the bot's direct bump push
# ("3 of 3 required status checks are expected" — enforce_admins + strict since
# 2026-09-29), so the bump lands as a PR the machine reviews, validates and
# merges. The tag + GitHub Release are cut from the merged 'chore(release):'
# commit by scripts/tag_release.sh (the `release-tag` job) — a tag push with the
# RELEASE_PAT still fires the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs.
#
# Changelog rules:
# - a curated `## Unreleased` section becomes the new version's notes;
# - otherwise notes are generated from commit subjects since the last tag;
# - a fresh empty `## Unreleased` is appended at the end.
#
# Idempotent: an open release PR whose branch tree already matches the computed
# bump is left alone (the 2h cron and racing pushes re-run this harmlessly).
set -euo pipefail

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

# Coalescing guards: pub.dev rate-limits publishes (~12/day), so releases are
# capped at one per 2h; runs with nothing new since the last tag are skipped.
git fetch origin main --tags --quiet
last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then
  pending=$(git rev-list --count "$last_tag..origin/main")
  if [ "$pending" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: nothing new since $last_tag, skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag") ))
  if [ "$tag_age" -lt 7200 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: coalesced — $last_tag is ${tag_age}s old (<2h); $pending commit(s) pending. Next eligible push or the 2h cron will release them."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# One release PR at a time; and if the previous bump merged but its tag hasn't
# been cut yet (release-tag job is still running its quality gate), wait —
# tagging the next bump before the previous one would mis-tag the range.
# Keyed on the PUBSPEC VERSION, not the head commit subject: a missed
# release-tag run must not wedge auto-release forever (any interleaved or
# non-squash merge changes the subject but not the version), so after 1h the
# guard lets a fresh bump absorb the untagged one instead of blocking.
open_release_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --json headRefName \
  --jq '[.[].headRefName | select(startswith("chore/release-v"))] | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "${open_release_prs:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
  echo "Auto-release: an open release PR is already queued for the machine — skipping."
  exit 0
fi
head_version=$(git show origin/main:pubspec.yaml | sed -n 's/^version: //p')
if [ -n "$head_version" ] && ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$head_version^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  head_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct origin/main) ))
  if [ "$head_age" -lt 3600 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged (release-tag job pending, ${head_age}s old) — skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "Auto-release: v$head_version merged but untagged for ${head_age}s — release-tag likely wedged; proceeding so the next range absorbs it."
fi

# chore:pin marks machine-created release PRs (gh-1134). Labeling is hygiene:
# if the label is missing from the repo, warn loudly and ship the PR anyway —
# the release is the payload, the label must never block it.
label_args=()
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi

for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  git fetch origin main
  git reset --hard origin/main

  current=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
  # Other workflows (iOS/macOS CI) tag releases without bumping pubspec —
  # when tags raced ahead, bump from the latest tag instead, or every run
  # dies on "tag already exists".
  latest_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$latest_tag" ]; then
    tag_version="${latest_tag#v}"
    if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$current" "$tag_version" | sort -V | tail -1)" = "$tag_version" ]; then
      current="$tag_version"
    fi
  fi
  IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$current"
  next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
  echo "Auto-release: v$current -> v$next (attempt $attempt)"

  last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then range="$last_tag..HEAD"; else range="HEAD"; fi
  bullets=$(git log "$range" --pretty='- %s' --no-merges | grep -v '^- chore(release):' || true)
  [ -z "$bullets" ] && bullets="- Maintenance release."

  NEXT="$next" BULLETS="$bullets" python3 - <<'PY'
import os
import re

nxt = os.environ["NEXT"]
bullets = os.environ["BULLETS"].strip()
path = "CHANGELOG.md"
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
section = f"## {nxt}\n\n{bullets}\n"

m = re.search(r"^## Unreleased[ \t]*$", text, re.M)
if m:
    rest = text[m.end():]
    head = re.search(r"^## ", rest, re.M)
    body = rest[: head.start()] if head else rest
    tail = rest[head.start():] if head else ""
    if body.strip():
        # Curated Unreleased content becomes this release's notes.
        new_section = f"## {nxt}\n" + body.rstrip() + "\n"
    else:
        new_section = section
    text = text[: m.start()] + new_section + ("\n" + tail if tail else "")
else:
    text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n" + section

text = text.rstrip() + "\n\n## Unreleased\n"
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text)

  release:
    name: Auto-release (bump PR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Every push to main gets a release with an auto-incremented patch version
    # (0.1.x -> 0.1.y), coalesced to <=1 per 2h — pub.dev rate-limits publishes
    # (~12/day; hit on 2026-07-18). Release commits are skipped (loop guard).
    # Since 2026-09-29 protected main rejects direct bot pushes (enforce_admins
    # + strict: "3 of 3 required status checks are expected", live 14:53-21:06Z
    # failures), so this job OPENS the bump PR (scripts/auto_release.sh) and
    # the machine reviews/validates/merges it; release-tag below cuts the tag.
    # Scheduled runs catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):'))
      || github.event_name == 'schedule')
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      # auto_release.sh's gh calls (pr list / pr create) authenticate via the
      # PAT — the job env carries no GH_TOKEN by default, so without this
      # every call dies under set -e and no bump PR ever opens (BLOCK
      # finding on PR #1093, live review 2026-09-30).
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # PAT (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the publish job —
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger downstream workflow runs.
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Bump version, changelog, open release PR
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  # Cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release from the merged release PR (see
  # scripts/tag_release.sh). The bump now lands as a PR (protected main
  # rejects direct bot pushes), so the tag phase keys on the merged
  # 'chore(release):' squash commit instead of following the bump push
  # directly. Tag push rides RELEASE_PAT (checkout token) — GITHUB_TOKEN
  # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped binaries/publish jobs. Serialized
  # with the bump PR job via the release-main group: tag first, next bump after.
  release-tag:

Goal — auto-release PRs are created and refreshed WITH the `chore:pin` label (v1, initial)

One sentence: **`scripts/auto_release.sh` labels the automated release PR `chore:pin` on creation AND on the refresh path — today the flag is simply never passed, so every release PR (e.g. #1130) ships label-less.**

### Problem (verified, 2026-09-30)

- PR #1130 (`chore(release): v1.0.496`, machine-created) has **zero labels**.
- Root cause, exact: `scripts/auto_release.sh:158` — `gh pr create --base main --head "$branch" --title … --body …` — **no `--label` flag anywhere in the script** (`grep -n "label"` → no hits).
- The label EXISTS in the repo (`chore:pin` — `gh label list`), so this is a one-flag omission, not a label-taxonomy gap.
- The refresh path (branch re-pushed, PR already open) also never adds the label.

### Fix contract

1. `gh pr create … --label "chore:pin"` at `auto_release.sh:158`.
2. Refresh path (`gh pr list` finds an open PR): idempotent `gh pr edit <n> --add-label "chore:pin"` so older label-less PRs self-heal on the next refresh.
3. Label absence must fail visibly (script logs a warning) but never block the release PR itself — labeling is hygiene, the release is the payload.

### Backward compatibility invariants

- Release flow, versioning, tag job untouched — label only.
- No new labels created; uses the existing `chore:pin`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Fresh release branch: created PR carries `chore:pin`. (shell test or workflow dry-run on a test branch)
- **AC2** — Refresh path with an existing label-less PR: label added. 
- **AC3** — Label already present: no error, no duplicate.
- **AC4** — Regression: release flow end-to-end unchanged (existing auto-release tests green). (REG-1)

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- Shell-level test with stubbed `gh` (pattern already used in repo script tests) covering create / refresh / already-labeled (AC1–AC3).
- **REG-1** — existing auto-release workflow unchanged; a red REG blocks merge.

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Label deleted from the repo someday: warning logged, PR still created (contract 3).

## Non-goals

- No label taxonomy redesign; no auto-pin automation beyond the label.

## References

- Label-less example: PR #1130.
- Omission site: `scripts/auto_release.sh:158` (`gh pr create`), refresh branch just above it.
- Existing label: `chore:pin` (`gh label list`…

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: self-heal the label instead of warn-only (repo convention)**

The check-then-warn approach deviates from how every other label-dependent automation in this repo behaves — they all auto-create the label first:

- `scripts/daily_publish_report.sh:31` — `gh label create daily-publish … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh:30` — `gh label create "$label" … >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml:499` — `gh label create nightly-red --force …`

Applying the same pattern here keeps the stated contract (labeling never blocks the release — `|| true`) while making E1 self-heal permanently instead of requiring a human to run the remediation from the WARNING:

```bash
label_args=()
gh label create "chore:pin" --force --color 1D76DB \
  --description "Machine-created release PR (auto-release)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if gh label view "chore:pin" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  label_args=(--label "chore:pin")
else
  echo "Auto-release: WARNING: label 'chore:pin' missing from repo — release PRs will ship without it (fix: gh label create chore:pin)." >&2
fi
```

Two side benefits:
1. `--force` is an upsert (precedented by nightly.yml), so it is idempotent when the label exists.
2. It narrows the tiny race where the label is deleted between this check and `gh pr create --label` — today that fails the create hard under `set -e`, blocking the release (the one scenario the "must never block" contract doesn't currently cover).
3. The WARNING also becomes more accurate: `gh label view` fails identically for a transient auth/network error and a truly missing label, so today's message can misdiagnose ("missing from repo") — with the create-first approach the warning only fires when even the create failed.
